style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The last of the fifteen Songs of Ascents, and the briefest of them -- three verses and barely two dozen Hebrew words -- that close the pilgrimage at night. The pilgrims are leaving the temple, and they turn to the ones who will not leave: the Levites who stand through the night in the house of the LORD. Bless the LORD, they tell the night shift; lift your hands toward the holy place. And the night shift answers them with the blessing they came for: may the LORD bless you out of Zion, the Maker of heaven and earth -- 'you' in the singular, each pilgrim sent home by name. Praise goes up in the first two verses and blessing comes down in the third, which is what every act of worship has ever been. The Western church has sung it at Compline, the last office of the day, ever since Benedict's Rule fixed it there some fifteen hundred years ago.

1.text: A song of ascents. Come now, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who stand through the night in the house of the LORD!
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. Behold, bless [barak] ye the LORD [YHWH], all ye servants [ebed] of the LORD, which by night [layil] stand [amad] in the house [bayith] of the LORD.
1.notes: hinneh barekhu et-YHWH kol-abde YHWH (H1288, H5650), 'behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD': the last Song of Ascents, addressed to the night shift -- ha-omedim be-bet-YHWH ba-lelot (H5975, H1004, H3915): those who STAND in the house of the LORD in the nights, the Levites on watch (cf. 1 Chronicles 9:33). The pilgrims, leaving, hand the praise to the ones who stay up.

2.text: Lift your hands up in the holy place, and bless the LORD!
2.amp: Lift up [nasa] your hands [yad] in the sanctuary ['holiness', qodesh, the KJV margin], and bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH].
2.notes: seu-yedekhem qodesh (H5375, H3027, H6944): lift your hands in the holy place -- the KJV's 'sanctuary'; the bare noun can also be read 'toward the holy place' or, as the margin has it, 'in holiness' -- the raised hands of Psalm 141:2, the night's incense; u-barakhu et-YHWH (H1288), 'and bless the LORD'.

3.text: May the LORD bless you out of Zion -- the Maker of heaven and earth.
3.amp: The LORD [YHWH] that made [asah] heaven [shamayim] and earth [eretz] bless [barak] you out of Zion [Tsiyyon].
3.notes: yevarekhkha YHWH mi-Tsiyyon (H1288, H3068, H6726), 'may the LORD bless you from Zion': the night-watchmen answer the pilgrims with a blessing -- 'you' is singular, each traveler blessed by name as he goes down the hill. oseh shamayim va-aretz (H6213, H8064, H776), 'Maker of heaven and earth': the credential of Psalm 121:2 and 124:8, the last words of the Ascents. Blessing goes up in verses 1-2 and comes down in verse 3; that exchange is the whole liturgy.
